forecast-period.text: A high pressure system southwest of Tasmania is expected to linger there until early next week, whilst extending a ridge over eastern SA. A trough lies through the far northwest, weakening over the weekend. A trough of low pressure over WA is expected to move over SA early next week, while a cold front clips the southeast.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms about the far northwest during the afternoon. Possible showers on and east of the ranges. Maximum temperatures above average about the south and west, tending near average in the northeast. Southeast to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes.
Mostly dry, apart from a light shower or two about the southeast. Southeast to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes.

Showers and thunderstorms developing in the west during the late afternoon and evening. Possible showers near the eastern border. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average about the west coast and tending near average in the northeast. East to northeasterly winds, fresh at times, with local afternoon sea breezes.

Showers and possible thunderstorms about the west, extending about central and southeastern districts during the day. Maximum temperatures above average and well above average about the west. North to northeasterly winds, fresh at times, tending northwesterly ahead of a southerly change moving across the west during the day.

text.p: Showers and thunderstorms, clearing from west. Maximum temperatures above average. North to northeasterly winds, fresh at times, tending northwesterly ahead of a southerly change moving throughout during the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: 2 to 5 mm about the agricultural areas, increasing to 2 to 10 mm about southern coasts and ranges and the far northwest. The chance of 10 to 20 mm with a thunderstorms, most likely in the northwest. Less than 2 mm possible elsewhere.
